title: feat(core)!: retire DataScopeManager and its row-level filter types (objectui#7750)
body:
Fixes #7750
Clause-②: yes

Executes ruling `5564753628` on objectui#7750 (option C, maintainer 「同意」): `DataScopeManager` and its `RowLevelFilter` vocabulary are retired from `@object-ui/core`. No alias, no deprecation window. Implemented by the `domain:ui` seat 2 dispatch, session `https://claude.ai/code/session_014mXUNuFomfj24w7s1pZzhN`.

## Public surface removed (`@object-ui/core`)

| name | kind |
|:--|:--|
| `DataScopeManager` | class |
| `defaultDataScopeManager` | const (shared instance) |
| `RowLevelFilter` | type |
| `DataScopeConfig` | type (read only by the class's `registerScopeWithConfig`; nothing else in the repo read it, so it goes with the class) |

Kept: `ViewDataProvider` and every element data-source export in `data-scope/`, and the `export * from './data-scope/index.js'` line in the package barrel. `DataScope` / `DataContext` in `@object-ui/types` are not touched (not ruled).

## Files

- deleted: `packages/core/src/data-scope/DataScopeManager.ts` and its two tests `__tests__/DataScopeManager.test.ts`, `__tests__/DataScopeManager.hardening.test.ts`
- `packages/core/src/data-scope/index.ts`: the four-name export block removed; the module docblock now describes what the module still holds and says row-level security is not evaluated here
- `packages/core/README.md`: the "Data Scope" section becomes "Expressions" (`evaluateExpression` alone); the matching Features bullet follows
- `content/docs/guide/architecture-overview.md`: the `data-scope/` line in the directory map names what is left
- `scripts/check-doc-example-types.mjs`: the ledger row for the deleted class's `@example` is removed
- `packages/permissions/src/evaluator.ts`: the two docblock pointers to the deleted file are rewritten; they keep their point about the guard and cite only issues
- `packages/permissions/src/__tests__/evaluator.prototype-guard-8044.test.ts`: **outside the claim's file surface.** Its header docblock cited the deleted file by path and the class by name, the same dangling-pointer class as the two `evaluator.ts` pointers. Bounded in-place repair: same defect class, mechanical, no open PR touches the file (all 12 open PR file lists read), same gate family (the permissions suite already runs for `evaluator.ts`). Comment-only.
- `.changeset/7750-retire-datascopemanager.md`: `'@object-ui/core': minor` with a **BREAKING** body naming each removed export, "no replacement", and the migration (row-level security is the spec's `RowLevelSecurityPolicySchema` `using` CEL predicate, lowered to an ObjectQL filter, fail-closed). `minor`, not `major`, per this repo's AGENTS.md version section, enforced by `check-changeset-no-major`; precedent PR objectui#10453. One paragraph reconciles the three pending entries that describe the class (the two `core-datascope-*` entries and `permissions-evaluator-prototype-guard-8044`), which are not edited (`check-changeset-overwrite`).

## Premise checks on this base (`ab50ccc`)

- Consumers: `git grep -E "DataScopeManager|RowLevelFilter|defaultDataScopeManager|DataScopeConfig"` over the whole tree minus CHANGELOGs: on the head only the three pending changesets named above still hit. Lit control `ViewDataProvider`: 16 files.
- `DataContext` (`@object-ui/types`): with the class gone it has no implementer and no consumer in this repository, only its declaration and the types barrel. Not removed, not ruled.
- **Surface pin: none exists for `@object-ui/core`.** PR objectui#10426 (`1237ae4`) regenerated no artefact (its 25-file diff has no generated file); `scripts/dump-public-manifest.mjs` dumps the SDUI component manifest from a browser build, not package exports; no committed file lists core's exports (control: `composeElementDataSource` hits no json, snap or api file). The instruments that read core's export set are `check:readme-exports` (TypeScript `getExportsOfModule` on the built `dist/index.d.ts`) and `check:doc-examples` (its ledger). Both are shown red on the removal commit and green on the head below. There was nothing to regenerate.
